t: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, compensation for permanent total disablement is calculated as:
o: 50% of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor, or Rs 1,20,000 whichever is more
40% of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor
60% of monthly wages multiplied by the relevant factor, or Rs 1,40,000 whichever is more
e: Death: 50% of wages x relevant factor (min Rs 1.2 lakh); PTD: 60% of wages x relevant factor (min Rs 1.4 lakh); PPD is a percentage of the PTD amount.

t: A micro enterprise insures its factory under the Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha policy for Rs 4.5 crore while the actual value at risk is Rs 5 crore. A fire causes a loss of Rs 20 lakh. The insurer pays:
e: Under-insurance here is 10%; BSUS waives the condition of average where under-insurance does not exceed 15%, so the full loss is paid.

t: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, the no-fault relief payable for a fatal accident caused by handling of hazardous substances is:
o: Rs 25,000 plus reimbursement of medical expenses up to Rs 12,500
e: The Act's Schedule provides Rs 25,000 for death (Rs 25,000 for PTD, Rs 12,500 medical reimbursement) on a no-fault basis; larger claims may be pursued in court.

t: Which of the following is NOT one of the four public sector general insurance companies in India?
o: The New India Assurance Company Ltd
e: The four PSU general insurers are National, New India, Oriental and United India; LIC is the public sector life insurer.

t: Following the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, a claim application before the MACT must be filed within what period from the date of the accident?
e: The 2019 amendment restored a limitation period of six months under Section 166(3); earlier there was no time limit after 1994.

t: 'Increased value' insurance in marine cargo is taken to cover:
o: The appreciation in the value of goods between shipment and arrival
The customs duty on the goods
e: Increased value cover tops up the original insured value when the market value at destination is expected to exceed the invoice/CIF value.

t: A 'positions' type Fidelity Guarantee policy covers:
o: Employees individually named in the schedule
Any person holding a specified position (e.g. cashier, storekeeper), without naming individuals
e: Positions policies are useful where staff turnover is high; the guarantee attaches to the post rather than the person.

t: Which of the following perils is covered under Institute Cargo Clauses (C)?
o: Entry of sea water into the hold
e: ICC(C) covers major casualties including jettison, fire, stranding, collision and general average sacrifice; washing overboard, sea water entry and earthquake are ICC(B) perils.

t: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 (as amended), the minimum compensation payable in case of death of an employee is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Death compensation is 50% of monthly wages multiplied by the age factor or Rs 1,20,000, whichever is higher; for permanent total disablement the minimum is Rs 1,40,000.

t: A motor own damage claim is assessed at Rs 12,000 and the policy has a compulsory excess of Rs 1,000 and a voluntary excess of Rs 2,500. The insured receives:
e: Both the compulsory and voluntary deductibles are deducted from the assessed loss: 12,000 - 1,000 - 2,500 = Rs 8,500.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 Master Circular, treatment under AYUSH systems (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) in a health policy is to be covered:
o: Up to 25% of the sum insured
Up to the full sum insured without any sub-limit
e: The circular requires AYUSH treatment to be covered on par with allopathic treatment, up to the sum insured, without sub-limits.

t: A 'sub-limit' in a health insurance policy refers to:
o: A cap on the amount payable for a specified treatment or expense head (e.g. cataract) within the overall sum insured
The deductible under a top-up plan
The waiting period for specific diseases
e: Sub-limits restrict the payout for named procedures or heads such as room rent or cataract surgery, irrespective of the total sum insured.

t: For a vehicle more than 5 years old, the IDV is:
o: Arrived at by mutual agreement between the insurer and the insured
Fixed at 50% of the current ex-showroom price
Fixed at 40% of the original invoice price
Not required as such vehicles cannot be given own damage cover
e: The depreciation table runs only up to 5 years; beyond that IDV is mutually agreed, often with reference to surveyor assessment or market value.

t: Under the SFSP policy, damage caused by leakage from automatic sprinkler installations is excluded when it results from:
o: Accidental discharge due to a faulty sprinkler head
Repairs or alterations to the building or the sprinkler installation
e: Sprinkler leakage is covered except where caused by repairs/alterations to the building or installation, or by defects in construction known to the insured.

t: 'Particular average' in marine insurance means:
o: A deliberate sacrifice made for the common safety
A partial loss caused fortuitously by an insured peril and borne by the owner of the property damaged
Expenses incurred by the master to save the venture
A total loss of part of the cargo
e: Particular average is an accidental partial loss falling solely on the interest concerned, as distinct from general average which is shared by all interests.

t: A fire proposal for risk inception on 1 March is received along with a cheque on 5 March; the cheque is realised on 8 March. Under Section 64VB read with the Insurance Rules, the risk can attach from:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). When premium is paid by cheque, risk may be assumed from the date of receipt of the cheque provided it is subsequently honoured; cover cannot be backdated to 1 March.

t: Under the Bharat Griha Raksha policy, when the home building is insured, general home contents are automatically covered for:
o: 20% of the building sum insured subject to a maximum of Rs 10 lakh
10% of the building sum insured with no limit
25% of the building sum insured subject to a maximum of Rs 25 lakh
e: BGR provides in-built cover for general contents at 20% of the building sum insured, capped at Rs 10 lakh, without separate declaration.

t: In a valued marine cargo policy, the value stated in the policy is, in the absence of fraud:
o: Reviewable by the insurer at the time of claim
A maximum limit only, with actual value to be proved
Relevant only for total loss claims
Conclusive between insurer and insured as the insurable value
e: Marine policies are agreed value contracts; the fixed value is binding for both total and partial losses unless fraud is proved.

t: Which of the following accidental deaths would normally be PAYABLE under a standard Personal Accident policy?
o: Death while participating in a motor racing event
Death caused while under the influence of intoxicating liquor
Death in a crash while flying a private aircraft as pilot
Death as a fare-paying passenger in a scheduled commercial airline crash
e: Aviation risk is excluded except as a fare-paying passenger in a licensed aircraft; racing, intoxication and piloting are standard exclusions.

t: Under the SFSP policy, loss or damage caused by forest fire is:
o: Covered under the bush fire peril
Covered only if the insured's premises are within 100 metres of the forest
Covered subject to an excess of 5%
e: Bush fire is a covered peril, but destruction by forest fire is specifically excluded from the policy.

t: Under the Arogya Sanjeevani policy, the cumulative bonus for each claim-free year and its maximum are:
o: 5% of sum insured per year, maximum 50%
e: Arogya Sanjeevani provides a cumulative bonus of 5% of the sum insured per claim-free year, subject to a maximum of 50%.

t: Under the standard Personal Accident table of benefits, loss of one hand and loss of sight of one eye in the same accident is compensated at:
e: Loss of two limbs, two eyes, or one limb and one eye is treated as permanent total disablement and paid at 100% of CSI.

t: Under a 60% quota share treaty, the insurer writes a risk for Rs 50 lakh and suffers a loss of Rs 20 lakh. The reinsurer's share of the loss is:
e: In quota share the reinsurer takes the same fixed percentage of every loss as of every premium: 60% of Rs 20 lakh = Rs 12 lakh.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required for registering a general insurance company in India is:
e: The Insurance Act prescribes a minimum paid-up capital of Rs 100 crore for a life or general insurer (Rs 200 crore for a reinsurer).

t: Under the Institute Cargo Clauses 2009 transit clause, in the absence of earlier termination, cover ends on expiry of how many days after completion of discharge at the final port?
e: The duration clause terminates cover at delivery to the final warehouse, on allocation for storage, or 60 days after discharge overside at the final port, whichever first occurs.

t: Mr Sharma was diagnosed with diabetes one year before taking a health policy with a 36-month PED waiting period. In the second policy year he is hospitalised for diabetic complications. The claim is:
o: Not payable, as the PED waiting period is incomplete
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Diabetes is a declared pre-existing disease; claims arising from it are payable only after the 36 months of continuous coverage have been completed.

t: Under PMFBY, the indemnity level applicable to high-risk crops/areas is:
e: Indemnity levels of 70%, 80% and 90% correspond to high, medium and low risk districts/crops respectively.

t: A policyholder sells his insured car and is yet to buy a new one. The NCB earned can be preserved by obtaining an NCB reserving (retention) letter from the insurer, which remains valid for:
e: NCB belongs to the insured, not the vehicle; the reserving letter allows it to be applied to a replacement vehicle purchased within 3 years.

t: The percentage of sum insured on each policy that Indian general insurers must compulsorily cede to GIC Re (obligatory cession) as notified by IRDAI for recent years is:
e: The obligatory cession to GIC Re has been fixed at 4% of sum insured on each policy for 2023-24 onwards (it was 5% earlier).

t: Under the reinstatement value clause of a fire policy, until the insured actually reinstates the damaged property, the insurer's liability is limited to:
o: Nil, no payment is made until reinstatement is complete
The market (depreciated) value basis of indemnity
The full reinstatement cost as an advance
e: The RIV basis applies only when reinstatement is carried out; otherwise the claim is settled on the ordinary indemnity (market value less depreciation) basis.

t: At the time of sale of a new two-wheeler, the compulsory long-term third party cover to be taken is for:
e: Following the Supreme Court order of 2018, new two-wheelers require 5-year TP cover and new private cars 3-year TP cover.

t: A fire policy is issued against a cheque for the premium and the cheque is subsequently dishonoured. The position of the insurer is that:
o: The policy remains valid and premium is recoverable as a debt
The risk is deemed never to have attached and the policy is void ab initio
The policy is valid for 15 days from issue
The insurer must give 30 days notice before cancelling
e: Under Section 64VB no risk can be assumed unless premium is received; a dishonoured cheque means premium was never received, so no cover came into existence.

t: A Machinery Breakdown policy covers the insured machinery:
o: Whether at work or at rest, or being dismantled for cleaning, overhaul or shifting within the premises
Only after a maintenance contract is in force
e: MBD covers sudden and unforeseen physical damage from mechanical or electrical causes in all these situations, as long as the machinery is within the insured premises.

t: Under a Contractor's Plant and Machinery policy, the insured plant is covered:
o: Whilst at work or at rest or being dismantled for cleaning or overhauling at the site named in the schedule
e: CPM is an annual policy covering mobile plant and equipment against external accidental damage at the site(s) specified, in all the listed states.

t: War and strikes risks on marine cargo are covered by:
o: Attaching the Institute War Clauses and Institute Strikes Clauses at additional premium
The basic ICC(A) clauses without extra premium
A separate policy issued only by GIC Re
e: All ICC sets exclude war and strikes; cover is bought back through the Institute War Clauses (Cargo) and Institute Strikes Clauses (Cargo).

t: Under a Money Insurance policy, the 'money in transit' section covers cash:
o: While in transit between the insured's premises and bank, carried by the insured or authorised employees, up to the per-transit limit
While in transit by any person including couriers and customers
Only while being carried in an armoured van
e: Cash in transit is covered only when carried by the insured or authorised employees (or specified carriers); loss while entrusted to unauthorised persons is excluded.

t: Under the standard Arogya Sanjeevani policy, the waiting period for specified diseases/procedures such as cataract, hernia and joint replacement is:
e: Arogya Sanjeevani applies a 24-month specific waiting period for listed ailments, a 30-day initial waiting period and a PED waiting period.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

t: For the death benefit to be payable under a Personal Accident policy, death must occur as a result of the accident within:
o: 12 months of the date of the accident
30 days of the date of the accident
6 months of the date of the accident
Any time, without a time limit
e: Standard PA wordings require death (or disablement) to occur within 12 calendar months of the accidental bodily injury.

t: Under the Arogya Sanjeevani policy, room rent (excluding ICU) is restricted to:
o: 1% of sum insured per day with no cap
2% of sum insured per day subject to a maximum of Rs 5,000 per day
e: Arogya Sanjeevani caps room rent at 2% of SI (max Rs 5,000/day) and ICU charges at 5% of SI (max Rs 10,000/day).

t: As per IRDAI norms, appointment of a licensed surveyor is mandatory for a motor own damage claim where the estimated loss exceeds:
e: The threshold for compulsory surveyor appointment is Rs 50,000 for motor claims and Rs 1 lakh for other classes; below these the insurer may assess in-house.

t: Which type of reinsurance protects an insurer against an accumulation of many small losses from a single event, such as a cyclone affecting thousands of policies?
e: Catastrophe XoL responds when the aggregate of losses from one event exceeds the cedant's retention; proportional treaties merely share each risk.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.

t: An application for compensation arising out of a motor accident is made to the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal under which section of the MV Act, 1988?
e: Section 166 provides for applications for compensation to the Claims Tribunal by the injured person, owner of damaged property or legal representatives of the deceased.

t: Increased Cost of Working (ICOW) under a Consequential Loss (Fire) policy is payable:
o: Without any limit as long as it is incurred
Only if it exceeds 10% of the gross profit
Only for wages of additional staff
Only to the extent it avoids a reduction in turnover not exceeding the gross profit thereby saved (economic limit)
e: ICOW is additional expenditure necessarily incurred to avoid or reduce the fall in turnover, limited to the gross profit it preserves.

t: The Standard Fire and Special Perils policy covers how many named perils in its basic form?
e: SFSP covers 12 perils: fire, lightning, explosion/implosion, aircraft damage, RSMD, STFI, impact damage, subsidence/landslide, bursting of tanks/pipes, missile testing, sprinkler leakage and bush fire.

t: Where an insurer delays settlement of a claim beyond the stipulated period, it is liable to pay interest on the claim amount at a rate of:
o: 2% above the bank rate prevailing at the beginning of the financial year in which the claim is reviewed
e: IRDAI's Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations provide for interest at 2% above the bank rate for delayed settlement.

t: Which part of a fire policy contains the particulars specific to the insured, such as name, address, sum insured, period and premium?
e: The schedule individualises the standard printed wording with the risk-specific details; wording, conditions and exclusions are common to all policies of that class.

t: A Plate Glass insurance policy covers:
o: Scratching and chipping of the glass surface
Accidental breakage of fixed plate glass described in the schedule, including the cost of temporary boarding up
Breakage of glassware stock in a shop
Glass that was already cracked at inception
e: Plate glass insurance is an all-risks cover for accidental breakage of fixed glass; scratches, superficial damage and pre-existing cracks are excluded.

t: Under a Contractor's All Risks (CAR) policy, cover for the contract works commences:
o: From the date the contract is signed
When the insured items are unloaded at the site, or on the policy start date if later
From the date of laying of foundation
Only after the first progress payment is received
e: CAR cover attaches on commencement of work or unloading of the first items at the site (whichever is later) and continues until handover or expiry.
